title: Fixed Price sorts by value: highest first, then lowest first on the next click
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with the Settings - Parts permission.
  • Category {Category-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC45 cat) exists.
  • Fixed rule part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC45-1) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-A} with fixed price (for example 9000.00).
  • Fixed rule part {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC45-2) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-A} with fixed price (for example 100000.00).
  • Fixed rule part {Part-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC45-3) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-A} with fixed price (for example 10000.00).
  • Fixed rule part {Part-D} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC45-4) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-A} with fixed price (for example 90000.00).
  • No other fixed rule at {Location-A} has a fixed price of 9,000 or more.
  • You are on a page other than Pricing and the Pricing Search box is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings and click Pricing in the Parts group of the Settings menu.
  2. Click the Fixed rules tab.
  3. Wait until the loading indicator on the Fixed rules tab disappears.
  4. Click the Fixed Price column header.
  5. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  6. Read the Fixed Price arrow and the first four rows.
  7. Click the Fixed Price column header again.
  8. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  9. Read the Fixed Price arrow.
  10. Scroll to the end of the list.
  11. Read the last four rows.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 6: the Fixed Price arrow points down (highest first) and the first four rows read {Part-B}, {Part-D}, {Part-C}, {Part-A}: highest price first, by value (with the examples 100,000 > 90,000 > 10,000 > 9,000).
  • Step 6: the order is by value, not by the printed text. A text order would put a price starting with 9 (9,000 or 90,000) above 100,000.
  • Step 9: the Fixed Price arrow now points up (lowest first).
  • Step 11: the last four rows read {Part-A}, {Part-C}, {Part-D}, {Part-B}: lowest price first, so the four highest prices end the list in rising order (9,000 < 10,000 < 90,000 < 100,000).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11258; story SV-10136 (Story 3, Fixed Rules, sortable columns; story text re-synced to the PRD on 13 Oct 2026); PRD "Settings Pricing And Categories Sorting (Price/Category)", Confluence 578781186, version 21 (14 Oct 2026), S3-R8, S3-R9 (with S3-R4, S3-R5), §2 Sort arrows, §4 Key Decisions 'Fixed price opens on the highest price', read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 1.4 (Fixed rules - before and after), 13 Oct copy, unchanged on 14 Oct. Story SV-10136 acceptance criteria (re-synced 13 Oct 2026) agree: first click $10.00 before $9.00, second click $9.00 first. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Price/Category QA build exists). The technical plan of 13 Oct 2026 (FR-018, FR-020) says the first click on Fixed price sorts lowest first; PRD version 21 (14 Oct 2026, S3-R4, S3-R8) says highest first and is newer, so this case follows the PRD.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R8: “Fixed price sorts by value. Its first click puts the highest price first.”
  • S3-R9: “The second click on Fixed price puts the lowest price first.”
  • S3-R4: “When the user clicks a sortable column header that is not currently sorted, the list sorts by that column: A to Z for Part number and Category, highest first for Fixed price (S3-R8).”
  • S3-R5: “When the user clicks that same header again, the list re-sorts in the opposite direction.”
  • PRD §4 Key Decisions: “Fixed price opens on the highest price. Its first click puts the highest price first, like every money column in ShopView (Default Sorting, decided 2026-10-06).”
  • PRD §2 Sort arrows: “A sortable column header shows an arrow when it is the column being sorted. The arrow points up for ascending and down for descending.”
